title: Perovskite-R1 suggests precursor additives tested in solar-cell devices
summary: A domain-tuned QwQ-32B model generated precursor-additive suggestions. Researchers tested selected recommendations in perovskite solar-cell devices against controls and manually selected additives and report improved device performance and material stability in their tested conditions. Two tested suggestions were 3,5-difluoropyridine-2-carboxylic acid and 5-hydroxy-2-methylbenzoic acid. This does not establish industrial operating lifetime or broad superiority over expert-selected additives.
ai_technology: Perovskite-R1, instruction-tuned QwQ-32B large language model

evidence.tested: The primary article reports the study-specific material and measurement summarized here.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and commercial deployment are not established.
evidence.ai_role: The domain-tuned LLM proposes precursor additives; researchers design, synthesize and test selected additives in devices and stability experiments.
